title: Sales Enablement: Unified Playbook - Positioning, Competitive Briefs, Pitch Deck, Pricing Guidance, Case Studies, Security FAQ
author: Asha Patel
content:
Summary

This playbook provides a single reference for Redwood Inference sales and customer-facing teams covering: positioning and messaging, competitive briefings, a suggested pitch deck with speaker notes, pricing guidance and negotiation levers, short case studies with metrics, and a prospect-facing security FAQ. Use this as the canonical source for external presentations, RFP responses, and deal coaching.

1) Positioning and Messaging

Short pitch (elevator):
- Redwood Inference is a developer-first inference platform that makes LLM-powered features predictable and economical at production scale - across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.

Core value props (three pillars):
1. Production-grade performance and reliability: predictable latency, throughput scaling, and fallbacks to keep apps online.
2. Cost-aware serving: batching, KV/prefix caching, and quantization recommendations that reduce per-token cost without sacrificing quality.
3. Unified operational model: same API, rollout tooling, and observability across hosted, reserved (Dedicated), and private (VPC/on-prem) deployments.

Messaging differentiators (talking points):
- We optimize inference economics for product teams - not just model access.
- Built-in fallbacks and routing policies maintain availability when capacity or regions are constrained.
- Full stack observability at the token level for cost, latency, and error analysis.

Target personas and value mapping:
- Product/ML Engineer: faster time-to-prototype + predictable latency for production features.
- Platform/Infra Team: stable SLAs and predictable reserved capacity with autoscaling policies.
- Security/Compliance Lead: private deployment options, KMS/HSM integration, and audit logging.

2) Competitive Briefs (one-page summaries for common competitors)

Competitor: Hyperscale Cloud AI Managed Endpoints
- Typical strengths: deep cloud integrations, single-vendor billing, large region coverage.
- Redwood counter: Superior developer ergonomics for inference (token-level observability, model-specific perf profiles), cost controls (batching/quantization guidance), and unified runtimes for private deployments.

Competitor: LLM API Providers (focused on simple API + hosted models)
- Typical strengths: quick to integrate, attractive developer portals.
- Redwood counter: Better for production at scale - reserved capacity (Dedicated), private deployments, SLAs, and operational tooling to prevent regressions (evals + rollouts).

Competitor: Self-hosted Inference Runtimes / OSS stacks
- Typical strengths: full control, no vendor lock-in.
- Redwood counter: We remove ops overhead with an optimized runtime and orchestration while providing private deployment options and enterprise support. Provide clear TCO comparison with support and operational burden factored in.

Competitive battlecards (how to win objections):
- Objection: "We can self-host and save money."
  - Response: Show TCO with operational costs (SRE FTEs, time-to-delivery, perf regressions) and highlight Redwood Optimize recommendations that lower unit cost without needing in-house kernel optimization work.
- Objection: "We already use cloud-managed endpoints."
  - Response: Emphasize cost controls and predictable reserved capacity for bursty workloads plus private deployment for compliance-sensitive customers.

3) Pitch Deck Outline + Speaker Notes (recommended 10-12 slides)

Slide 1: Title / Prospect Logo
- Note: Keep simple; establish familiarity.

Slide 2: Agenda
- Note: Set expectations: problem, how Redwood solves it, validation, pricing, next steps.

Slide 3: Market & Problem
- Key bullets: explosion of LLM capabilities; serving, not model ownership, is the long-term bottleneck.

Slide 4: Redwood Inference Overview
- Mission, one-liner, deployment modes (hosted, Dedicated, Private).

Slide 5: How it works (runtime + orchestration)
- Speaker notes: mention kernel selection, KV caching, batching, smart routing, and fallback policies.

Slide 6: Performance & Economics (data-driven)
- Include sample benchmark: 95th pctl latency targets by model class, cost per 1M tokens with/without batching.

Slide 7: Security & Compliance
- Highlight KMS/HSM, audit logs, VPC options, SOC/ISO compliance status (link to security artifacts).

Slide 8: Case Studies (two short vignettes)
- See below for details and metrics.

Slide 9: Pricing Models & Example Econ
- Show self-serve hosted pricing and Dedicated reserved capacity examples with units and sample invoice math.

Slide 10: Implementation Plan / Timeline
- Typical 6-8 week plan for pilot -> production with checkpoints for evals and SLA kick-in.

Slide 11: Next Steps & Ask
- Pilot sign-up, POC success metrics, stakeholders to include.

Slide 12: Appendix / Technical Q&A

4) Pricing Guidance and Negotiation Levers

Pricing models (standard):
- Hosted (usage-based): per-generation-token and per-embedding-unit pricing.
- Dedicated (committed capacity): monthly reservation with baseline throughput and optional burst credits.
- Private (enterprise licensing): platform fee + yearly support and optional on-prem packaging.

Example pricing table (illustrative):
- Hosted (text gen): $0.006 / 1K input tokens; $0.012 / 1K output tokens.
- Embeddings: $0.02 / 1K embedding units.
- Dedicated: $X / GPU-month reserve (negotiable by term).

Negotiation levers and recommended concessions:
- Commit term and volume: offer stepped discounts at 6 / 12 / 24-month terms.
- Early payment or annual prepay: 3-7% discount depending on size.
- Implementation professional services: include 20-40 hours of onboarding assistance for enterprise pilots.
- Observability add-ons: additional retention or custom dashboards as premium upsell.

Price objection playbook:
1. Re-anchor on unit economics (cost per 1M tokens with Redwood Optimize changes vs current baseline).
2. Tie committed discounts to measurable SLAs (latency/availability).
3. Offer a short-term pilot with capped spend and a transition credit if they convert to Dedicated.

5) Case Studies (short, customer-facing blurbs)

Case study A: "Converso - Customer Support Triage"
- Customer profile: mid-market SaaS, 120 engineer org, handles 30k support tickets/month.
- Use case: contextual triage and suggestion generation for support agents.
- Deployment: Hosted -> Dedicated reserve for peak support hours.
- Outcome: 40% reduction in average handle time, 2x reduction in external search calls, estimated $250k annualized savings in support operations.
- Metrics used in deal: latency 95p < 200ms for short prompts; cost per 1M tokens reduced by 35% after batching and caching.

Case study B: "FinSecure - Regulated On-prem Assistant"
- Customer profile: financial services firm with strict data residency and audit requirements.
- Use case: internal knowledge assistant for compliance and contract review.
- Deployment: Private (VPC + on-prem package), KMS integration, audit logging enabled.
- Outcome: passed internal audit for data residency, reduced manual review hours by 30%, enabled quicker contract turnaround.

6) Security FAQ for Prospects (top 12 questions)

Q1: Can we deploy Redwood in our VPC or on-prem?
A1: Yes. Redwood Private supports VPC deployments and on-prem packaging for air-gapped environments. We provide a private control plane and integrations with KMS/HSM.

Q2: What compliance certifications do you hold?
A2: We maintain SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 readiness; additional compliance evidence is available under NDA. Contact security@redwood.ai for audit artifacts.

Q3: How is customer data isolated?
A3: For Dedicated and Private deployments, data storage and logs are segregated per-customer. Hosted data-at-rest is encrypted and access-controlled; see our data-residency policy for regional constraints.

Q4: Do you support customer-managed keys?
A4: Yes - KMS integrations (AWS KMS, GCP KMS) and HSM options for Private deployments.

Q5: How long do you retain logs and telemetry?
A5: Default telemetry retention is 90 days; extended retention plans are available as an add-on. Audit logs for Private deployments can be kept per customer policy.

Q6: Do you allow model auditing and explainability tooling?
A6: We provide request/response logging and tooling to attach eval prompt-sets and regressions. We also support feature flags and rollout audits.

Q7: How do you handle PII and sensitive data?
A7: Customers can opt-in to data-handling policies: (1) no data retention for hosted requests, (2) redaction pipelines, or (3) Private deployment where data never leaves customer network.

Q8: Is there an incident response process?
A8: Yes. We maintain an incident response runbook and will notify customers per our SLA. See our incident response page for timelines and contact procedures.

Q9: What SLAs are offered?
A9: Hosted services have best-effort SLAs; Dedicated contracts include uptime and latency targets (negotiated per contract). Contact your AE for specifics and historical performance dashboards.

Q10: How are third-party models / open models handled?
A10: We provide a curated model catalog with provenance and performance profiles. Model licensing and usage constraints are documented per model entry.

Q11: Can we run private inference with custom models?
A11: Yes - Private deployments support customer model artifacts; our onboarding team will validate compatibility and provide kernel/quantization guidance.

Q12: Who is the security contact for prospect discussions?
A12: Security pre-sales: security@redwood.ai (response SLA 48 hours). For enterprise deals, we can arrange an architecture review with the security team.

7) Implementation & Typical Timelines

Pilot plan (6-8 weeks):
- Week 0: Kickoff, define success metrics and dataset/prompt sets.
- Week 1-2: Integration and baseline metrics collection.
- Week 3-4: Optimize batching/caching, implement KV prefixes and quantization profile suggestions.
- Week 5-6: Q/A, run production canary, finalize SLA terms and handover to customer SRE.

Owner & escalation path
- Sales Owner: AE assigned to deal.
- Technical Owner: Solutions Engineer for POC & on-call during pilot.
- Security/Escalation: Security pre-sales (security@redwood.ai).

Contact sheet:

Sample pilot success criteria (example list):
- Latency 95p < 250ms for 90% of production prompts.
- Reduction in per-token cost >= 20% through batching/caching within pilot window.
- No PII exfiltration incidents; audit log completeness verified.
